View Dr. Arnold’s Resources ›

Referral Inquiry

## Submit an Oncology Referral Inquiry

Please complete the form below and our team will follow up with next steps. If you are unsure which oncologist or location is the best fit, select “Unsure” where applicable.

Questions

## Common Referral Questions

##### Can my clinic refer a patient if we are not an oncology host hospital?

Yes. Clinics that do not host MOVES oncology service days can submit a referral inquiry, and the MOVES team will help direct the case to the appropriate oncology location.

##### How do oncology host hospitals schedule patients?

Hospitals with confirmed MOVES oncology service days can use their clinic portal to schedule patients within their designated oncology appointment block.

##### Can pet owners schedule directly with MOVES oncology?

Pet owners should start by speaking with their primary veterinarian. Referring clinics can submit an inquiry or contact MOVES for guidance on the appropriate next step.

## Information for Referring Veterinarians

If a referred patient is an emergency case, please complete the following steps. 

Small animal patients

  * If your veterinary clinic plans to refer a patient with a life-threatening condition to the VMC's small animal emergency and critical care service, please call 306-966-7126 in advance (regardless of the time, day or night) so the VMC clinical team can discuss the case, determine if the hospital is able to accept the case, and provide potential costs and timelines. 
  * If it is a life-threatening emergency and a member of the VMC clinical team is unable to talk to you within five minutes, please go ahead and send the case to the hospital.

What to expect

While the WCVM Veterinary Medical Centre (VMC) shares many similarities to other veterinary hospitals, there are some differences that may have an impact on your appointment.

The VMC is a teaching hospital for WCVM veterinary students and for students enrolled in the veterinary technology program at the Saskatchewan Polytechnic. Please note that teaching takes additional time. Students participate in all aspects of examining and treating our patients under the immediate supervision of licensed veterinarians and board-certified veterinary specialists. While teaching is essential to our facility, the well-being of our patients is the highest priority for VMC clinical teams.

Given the complexity of referral cases, we often need to order additional diagnostic testing or consult with others about diagnoses and treatment plans for patients. If you are travelling from out of town, please be prepared to stay two days in Saskatoon with your animal. In some cases, your stay may need to be longer.

During your appointment, we will give you an estimate of the length of time it may take for additional tests and consultation.

# Pharmacy

# About

The WCVM Veterinary Medical Centre operates an on-site veterinary pharmacy that provides services to all VMC clients and western Canadian animal owners.

The pharmacy's professional staff members also work closely with the medical centre's medical oncology service to provide chemotherapy to oncology patients.

### Prescription Refills

If you are a VMC client and wish to refill your animal's prescription, please contact the VMC Pharmacy at 306-966-7120.

Dr. Schuh completed a rotating internship in small animal medicine and surgery at the University of Illinois (2013) and an oncology internship at Veterinary Specialty Hospital of San Diego (2014). She is exceptionally proud of her time leading the veterinary clinical trials team at The Ohio State University in cutting-edge research (2015-2016) and completing her residency in medical oncology here at Veterinary Cancer Group (2016-2019). She received board certification in the summer of 2021. Dr. Schuh is thrilled to continue her time at Veterinary Cancer Group and practices in the Los Angeles office. Her professional interests include the human-animal bond, small molecular inhibitors/targeted therapies, and advancing the veterinary profession through clinical trials and translational medicine. When she is not at work, she is a food and wine enthusiast and is Corgi obsessed.

#### Cecile Siedlecki

DVM, DACVIM (Oncology)

Dr. Siedlecki worked as a chemist in the aerospace industry before returning to school to become a veterinarian, combining her love for science and the human-animal bond. She graduated from UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine and then went into general practice for 5 years before returning to complete a residency in medical oncology.
Dr. Siedlecki understands the worry and concerns clients have when their pets are diagnosed with cancer, so she spends time explaining the disease and treatment options. Dr. Siedlecki finds oncology rewarding when she can provide her patients with a high quality of life and develops a close rapport with the clients over the course of treatment.
Dr. Siedlecki and her wife, share their home with their dogs Cricket and Tortue.

#### Susan Feng

DVM, Diplomat ACVIM (Oncology)

Dr. Suzie Feng attended veterinary school at the University of Glasgow in Scotland. She then returned to California and pursued a rotating Internship at Veterinary Specialty Hospital North County, in San Diego, before beginning a 3-year medical oncology residency at the Veterinary Cancer Group in Tustin. She completed her residency program and became board-certified in Medical Oncology in 2025.

Dr. Feng loves seeing (and feeding) her patients and enjoys the long-term relationships she builds with them.

In her spare time, Dr. Feng likes to be outdoors and be active. However, she also loves a relaxing day at home, cuddling her little tripod dachshund or training her crazy Belgian Malinois.
